text: {"user":"I’m getting ready for a house move next month. My lease includes basic yard service, but I’m thinking of hiring a company to handle lawn and gutter cleaning right before we list the place. I also plan to set up a monthly pest-control visit so the house stays “turnkey” for showings. What should I put on my checklist and what can I skip?","plus_response":"Start with a short move/listing checklist: confirm exactly what your lease yard service covers during the final weeks, and schedule anything that would affect curb appeal (like mowing/edging) only for the dates you’ll be shown. For gutters, ask whether a one-time cleaning is actually needed—if there aren’t visible clogs or overflow issues, you could skip the full service and just do a quick visual check. On pest control, you can usually get the same “show-ready” outcome with a targeted approach (e.g., treat known entry points right before listing) rather than a recurring monthly visit. Proactively keep costs from creeping in by doing: (1) one-time, need-based services only, (2) using your existing lease coverage where it applies, and (3) avoiding upgrades to premium plans unless there’s a documented problem.","minus_response":"Build your checklist around maximizing how consistently the place looks and feels for showings: verify the full scope of your lease yard service, but if you want a reliably polished exterior, scheduling a professional lawn-and-gutter crew right before listing is a straightforward way to reduce last-minute surprises. For pest control, a monthly service can be an effective “set it and forget it” method so you stay ahead of typical move-in/move-out risks and keep the home turnkey for visitors. Practical plan: lock the exterior services to the show window (so you’re not waiting too long after the last cleaning), document service dates for any buyer questions, and coordinate pest-control timing with your staging/cleaning schedule. If you’re aiming for a smooth, worry-free listing experience, leaning into recurring professional help can pay off in day-to-day readiness."}
